With a 3 round burst; for every trigger squeeze, you get 3 rounds. Then you have to release the trigger, it resets, and you can shoot another 3 rounds. If you have a fast finger, though, it can still seem like full auto as there will be little discernible difference between release the trigger after the burst, and the weapon having a full auto setting. You just won’t really hit anything man-sized, unless it’s by luck. With a 30 round magazine, you can only do that trick 10 times before you have to reload (Vietnam era mags were 20 rounds).

Full auto is technically primarily for suppressing fire. That’s better accomplished with belt-fed, crew served weapons, though if you have a squad of dudes, shooting with a burst, full auto, or even just a standard semi-auto, will keep most heads down, and shooting semi-auto means you can have better control of where your rounds go.
